items.title: Meghan Markle Eyes Acting Return After Move Back to the U.K.
items.summary:
Meghan Markle is considering a return to acting as she and Prince Harry prepare to move back to Britain after six years in California. Variety confirmed that the Duchess of Sussex is weighing a screen comeback, following a report from the Australian outlet News.com.au that she has been offered a role in a project shooting in the U.K.

People close to the couple have not disputed the report, though no details about the project have been made public. The interest follows Wednesday's announcement that the Sussexes are leaving Montecito for an extended stay in England, a decision that caught most observers off guard.

Meghan's acting career centers on Suits, where she played paralegal-turned-lawyer Rachel Zane across seven seasons from 2011 to 2018. She stepped away from the profession after marrying Harry that year, though she is set to appear as herself in Close Personal Friends, an Amazon MGM comedy starring Brie Larson and Lily Collins.

Her recent work has been closer to lifestyle programming than scripted television. She hosted the Netflix series With Love, Meghan, which served as a launchpad for her brand As Ever, and turned up as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia.

The family is expected in Britain within weeks, with Archie and Lilibet starting school in September. The couple will keep their Montecito home and have no plans to move Archewell or As Ever across the Atlantic, and they remain non-working royals following their 2020 departure from official duties.

items.title: Prince Harry, Elton John and More Ordered to Pay Initial $13 Million to Daily Mail Publisher After Losing Privacy Case
items.summary:
A British judge has ordered Prince Harry, Elton John, Liz Hurley and four others to pay an initial £9.54 million, roughly $13 million, in legal costs to Associated Newspapers, publisher of the Daily Mail, after their privacy case against the company collapsed. The group has seven days to hand over the money.

Also named in the order are John's husband David Furnish, Simon Hughes, Sadie Frost and Baroness Doreen Lawrence. Associated is pursuing a total costs order of £34.4 million. Justice Nicklin has not decided whether the group will be liable for the full sum, which he described as excessive, but on Friday he ruled that costs should be assessed on an indemnity basis and declined to impose a cap, saying a cap would risk unfairness.

The claimants had sued Associated over allegations of unlawful information gathering. Nicklin threw out the case in full last month in a 436-page judgment, finding the group had not proved its claims. "In significant respects the case shifted from the pleaded allegation of lies to broader criticisms of Associated's inquiries, disclosure and corporate response to the Leveson Inquiry," he wrote. "This is not how allegations of this seriousness should be advanced."

As Variety reported, the publisher had sought more than £9.9 million as an interim payment ahead of future hearings on total costs, while lawyers for the group argued for £7.9 million, according to the BBC. Dozens of witnesses testified at trial, including Harry, who flew in from the United States to appear in person.

After last month's ruling, Harry and Lawrence, whose son Stephen was murdered in 1993, said in a joint statement: "We came to Court seeking justice and accountability. But we have received neither. It is a complete and obvious whitewash, but sadly not altogether unexpected." Associated called Friday's interim costs order "a devastating critique of an attempt to destroy a newspaper and the reputations of its journalists, editors and executives."

The bill lands days after Harry and Meghan Markle announced they are returning to the U.K. with their two children.

items.title: Jon Landau Remembers ‘Generous Friend’ and Springsteen Biographer Dave Marsh
items.summary:
Jon Landau, Bruce Springsteen's longtime manager and a former Rolling Stone writer, has published a tribute to the critic and biographer Dave Marsh, who died Aug. 14 at his home in Norwalk, Connecticut. Marsh was 76. The cause has not been determined.

Marsh was an early editor at Creem and later wrote for Rolling Stone, The Village Voice and Newsday, producing more than 25 books over his career, among them Before I Get Old: The Story of the Who and Born to Run: The Bruce Springsteen Story. Landau posted his remembrance to social media, and Springsteen shared it.

In the tribute, published by Rolling Stone, Landau described Marsh at 19 helping build Creem in Detroit as "a punk alternative to Rolling Stone's early hegemony in the emerging world of rock mags," then joining that same magazine at 22. The two argued about music, politics and writing every time they met. "We continued doing that through thick and thin for most of the next fifty years," Landau wrote.

Marsh succeeded Landau as editor of Rolling Stone's record section, where Landau said he engaged in regular "hand-to-hand combat" with co-founder Jann Wenner. "They usually fought each other to a draw," he wrote. Landau called Marsh "a generous friend" born with "the DNA of a confrontationalist" alongside "a caring heart, a love for people, and a desire to do good whenever and wherever he could."

Landau singled out the first Springsteen biography as the work where Marsh "found his truest metier," writing that fifty years on it remains the essential account of the singer's early years. Marsh also helped create E Street Radio and hosted Kick Out the Jams on SiriusXM for nearly two decades.

Closest to Marsh's heart, Landau wrote, was the Kristen Ann Carr Fund, founded with his wife Barbara Carr after her daughter Kristen died of cancer in 1991 at 21. The couple organized benefit shows for more than three decades, often featuring Springsteen. "Countless doctors were trained, in no small measure, due to Dave's efforts," Landau wrote, closing: "I will miss him for the rest of my life."

items.title: Earth, Wind, & Fire Shares Health Update on Drummer John Paris: ‘Our Hope Is Strong’
items.summary:
Earth, Wind & Fire has given a new update on drummer John Paris, who was placed in a medically induced coma this month after a critical medical emergency. Paris, 58, has woken up again and remains in intensive care, where he faces two major surgeries.

A representative for band member Verdine White shared the news with People, as Rolling Stone reported. "Since our last few updates, there have been both encouraging moments and new challenges," the rep said. "As we've said from the beginning, recovery isn't a straight line, and John's journey continues to remind us of that every day." Paris had briefly regained consciousness earlier before doctors sedated him again.

His wife, Kathy Merrick, told People that the drummer is fighting daily. "This journey is definitely a marathon, but JP is fighting every single day and our hope is strong," she said. "John has already overcome obstacles that once seemed impossible, and while there is still a long road ahead, each step forward gives everyone around him renewed hope."

The emergency happened on Aug. 6, hours before Earth, Wind & Fire was set to perform in San Francisco alongside Lionel Richie. The band postponed the show and said it hoped to reschedule, apologizing to ticket holders for "the unexpected change" without naming who had been hospitalized.

White's wife, Shelly Clark White, and family friend Tazz Cole later confirmed the details on Facebook, explaining that the privacy had been deliberate until information began circulating publicly. A friend of Merrick has since started a GoFundMe for Paris and his wife, asking fans and the music community to return the generosity the couple has shown over the years.

items.title: Def Leppard’s Vivian Campbell Reveals His Cancer Has Returned
items.summary:
Def Leppard guitarist Vivian Campbell says his cancer has returned after a donor transplant failed to take. Campbell, who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma in 2013 and had been in remission, disclosed the setback during an interview with El Salvador's Radio YSKL FM.

Campbell explained that his condition worsened sharply two years ago. "In the winter of 2023, I got really scared about what was happening and the pace at which it was happening," he said, adding that a donor transplant became "my only hope to survive." He underwent the procedure in January 2025. "Unfortunately, it didn't stick. So the cancer has returned. And I'm continuing treatments to manage it."

The guitarist said he expects to need a second transplant with a different donor within a few years, but has no intention of pulling back in the meantime. Alongside Def Leppard and his other band Last in Line, he has taken up rally driving, a longtime ambition. "As a child, I thought, 'If I don't play guitar for a living, I'm gonna be a race car driver,'" he said.

Campbell framed continued work as central to how he has handled more than a decade of treatment. "Even when I was at a really low ebb with cancer treatment, the fact that I could still continue to work, that gives me something to live for," he said, contrasting that with people he has known who "only focused on" a diagnosis. He also credited catching the disease early, saying it has "always been more about managing my cancer."

Consequence reported the news, citing a transcription of the radio interview by Blabbermouth. Campbell has missed a handful of Def Leppard dates in 2024 and 2025 because of his health. The band has a show scheduled in Hollywood, Florida on Oct. 15, followed by a Latin American tour.
